solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What's behind single road block?

parts.note: behind is slang for the backside, an ass
single means one, the Roman numeral I
ST is the abbreviation for street, a road

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what sits behind a lone roadblock.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble says every across definition has something in common: each is the opposite of its answer, so 'block' defines its antonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonym, as the preamble requires: to obstruct is the reverse of giving help.

clue.text: Princess wants location of treasure — is that appropriate?

parts.note: Princess Anne is the British Princess Royal
X marks the spot on a treasure map

explanation.surface: A princess wants to know where the treasure lies and whether that is fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to seize territory or take it over for oneself.

clue.text: It's not a silly place

indicators.note: silly signals that the preceding words are jumbled foolishly

explanation.surface: Reassurance that somewhere is a sensible spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' may suggest a cricket fielding position, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a post or position where someone is placed.

clue.text: One kiss blown by idiot Blair — excuse my French

indicators.note: blown means removed, and idiot means the remaining letters are muddled

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
X is the conventional sign for a kiss

explanation.surface: The prime minister foolishly blows a kiss and swears in French.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I and X out of BLAIR EXCUSE and rearrange the rest. 'excuse my French' looks like the apology but 'excuse' is fodder; 'my' is an exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: A French oath: this exclamation serves as a Gallic 'my goodness'.

clue.text: What's bad about marines being cold?

indicators.note: about means the scrambled letters go round the marines
bad signals that the word what is spoiled into a new order

parts.note: the 's is just 'is', a link, leaving the word what as fodder
RM is the abbreviation for the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: Asking what is so wrong about marines feeling the chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' turns WHAT into WATH, which goes 'about' RM. Like every across clue, the definition is the opposite of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonym, as the preamble requires: chilliness is the reverse of heat.

clue.text: In the air force there's much to take in

indicators.note: to take in means the word for much holds the next letter

parts.note: a lot means much

explanation.surface: Air force life gives you plenty to absorb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air force' reads as one phrase, but 'air' ends the definition and 'force' gives F.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: overhead, up high off the ground.

clue.text: Shepherd sees sheep climbing mostly fragile rock

indicators.note: climbing reverses a word in a down clue, as it reads upward

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep

indicators.note: mostly means the final letter of the rock is dropped

parts.note: shale is a crumbly layered rock

explanation.surface: A shepherd watches a sheep scrambling up loose rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns RAM to MAR; 'mostly' drops the last E of SHALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verbs: to guide or herd people into order.

clue.text: Doubt the man's bitter having secured bronze

parts.note: the man's is he's, HES

indicators.note: having secured means the bitter word holds the colour inside

parts.note: icy means bitterly cold
tan is a bronze colour

explanation.surface: Suspecting a sour man got his medal in third place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bronze' suggests a medal but is the colour TAN; 'bitter' means freezing, ICY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: uncertainty or reluctance before acting.

clue.text: Reduce points — risk losing lead

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north

indicators.note: losing lead means the first letter of the word for risk is dropped

parts.note: to risk is to chance something

explanation.surface: Advice to cut points and stop gambling on going in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing lead' drops the C of CHANCE, leaving HANCE. The across definitions are all opposites of their answers.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonym, as the preamble requires: to diminish is the reverse of to improve or increase.

clue.text: An unknown number of us sort of starve

parts.note: N stands for an unspecified number in mathematics
belonging to us is ours, OUR
the suffix -ish means sort of, as in greenish

explanation.surface: A vague number of people are rather going hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: As in all the across clues, the definition is the antonym of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonym, as the preamble requires: depriving of food is the reverse of feeding well.

clue.text: A visa arranged upon entry?

parts.note: a means per, as in once a day

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of visa are put in a new order

parts.note: upon means on

explanation.surface: A travel visa sorted out on arrival in a country.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'entry' means seeping in, not arrival at a border.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: permeation, a spreading in throughout.

clue.text: Old glue will keep it quiet

parts.note: EX means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: will keep means the glue holds the next word inside it

parts.note: cement is a glue or binding agent

explanation.surface: Old adhesive will keep something hushed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep it quiet' reads as an idiom, but 'keep' belongs to the container and only 'quiet' defines, as the opposite of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonym, as the preamble requires: calm stillness is the reverse of thrilled agitation.

clue.text: Be besotted with the one fronting Heaven 17

indicators.note: the one fronting means the letter at the front of the following word

parts.note: the answer to 17 down, meaning troubled or gnawed at, gives ATE, as in what's eating you

explanation.surface: Being infatuated with the singer leading the band Heaven 17.
explanation.walkthrough: Heaven 17 is a British synth-pop band, but here 17 is a cross-reference to 17 down. The definition is the opposite of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonym, as the preamble requires: being infatuated is the reverse of loathing.

clue.text: Starting to find river's hidden current

indicators.note: hidden means the next word is concealed within the river

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall, England
in means fashionable, current

explanation.surface: Beginning to discover a river's concealed flow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like a river's flow but means IN, fashionable. The definition is the opposite of the answer, like every across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonym, as the preamble requires: beginning is the reverse of ending or last.

clue.text: Concern about what hoax is not — a reason to call 999

indicators.note: about means the company wraps around the other letters

parts.note: a concern is a business, a firm
a hoax is not genuine, real

explanation.surface: Worry that a call is genuine, prompting an emergency phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 999 is the UK emergency phone number.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a bell warning of flames is a prompt to ring the emergency services.

clue.text: Harmless sport featured in horrible books

indicators.note: featured in means the sport sits inside the word for horrible

parts.note: vile means horrible
RU is rugby union, a sport
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: An innocuous game appearing in some dreadful books.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the opposite of the answer, as in every across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonym, as the preamble requires: innocuous is the reverse of poisonous or deadly.

clue.text: Reject help when turning into celebrity

indicators.note: into means the turned help goes inside the word for celebrity

parts.note: repute is fame or celebrity

indicators.note: turning means the word for help is read backwards

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: Turning down a famous person's offer of assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes DIA from AID, which goes 'into' REPUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to disown or refuse to accept.

clue.text: Families around with new children

indicators.note: around means the families go round the other letters

parts.note: families are groups, as in language families

explanation.surface: Families gathered round together with their new offspring.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the opposite of the answer, like all the across clues.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonym, as the preamble requires: youngsters are the reverse of adults.

clue.text: Afraid of Romeo that is breaking promise

indicators.note: breaking means the other letters split the promise open

parts.note: giving your word is a promise
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Scared of Romeo, who is breaking his vow.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: anxious, fearful.

clue.text: Retiring? What's wrong about retiring?

indicators.note: about signals that the word for what's wrong is turned round

parts.note: what's up means what's wrong, so up means wrong
retiring means bashful, shy

explanation.surface: Asking a timid person what troubles them about being timid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns UP into PU. The first 'Retiring' defines by its opposite, as every across clue does; the second gives SHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonym, as the preamble requires: bashful and modest is the reverse of forward and assertive.

clue.text: Companion's feeding of star pupil

indicators.note: feeding means the companion goes into the other word

parts.note: solar means of the sun, a star
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A companion's coaching of a top student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star pupil' reads as one phrase; 'star' belongs to SOLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a student or learner.

clue.text: Dark area surrounded by wood

indicators.note: surrounded by means the area letter sits inside the wood

parts.note: fir is a tree and its timber, a wood

explanation.surface: A shadowy patch enclosed by trees.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the opposite of the answer, as in every across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonym, as the preamble requires: pale or light-coloured is the reverse of dark.

clue.text: Tabloid design has to be red

indicators.note: design means the letters of the following words are laid out anew

explanation.surface: A newspaper layout that must be printed in red.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the opposite of the answer, like all the across clues; a red-top is a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonym, as the preamble requires: the large-format serious newspaper is the reverse of the small popular one.

clue.text: Security guards start to smoke herb

indicators.note: guards means the security wraps around the next letter

parts.note: bail is money given as security for release

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Security staff guard a smoker beginning a cigarette among herbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a fragrant leaf used in cooking.

clue.text: Immature like a nobleman?

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman
the suffix -y means like, as in earthy

explanation.surface: Asking whether childishness is aristocratic.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: premature, not yet developed.

clue.text: Exotic bird coated in spice, which is most normal

indicators.note: coated in means the bird is wrapped in the spice

parts.note: zest is spice or piquancy
the ani is a tropical American cuckoo

explanation.surface: A foreign bird covered in seasoning, the most ordinary dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the opposite of the answer, as every across definition is.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonym, as the preamble requires: most ordinary is the reverse of most crazy.

clue.text: Footballers need one to attract success

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, England's football body
one is the Roman numeral I
to lure is to attract

explanation.surface: A football team needs a player who will draw victories.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the opposite of the answer, like every across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonym, as the preamble requires: triumph is the reverse of a flop.

clue.text: You might say an FT setter will make things clear

indicators.note: you might say signals that the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: Mudd is a Financial Times setter, so Mudd'll means Mudd will

explanation.surface: A Financial Times setter promises to clarify matters.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the opposite of the answer, as in all the across clues.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonym, as the preamble requires: clarifying is the reverse of confusing.

clue.text: Bank of Scotland over in Gotham, miles away

indicators.note: in means the reversed bank sits inside the city

parts.note: Gotham is a nickname for New York, NY

indicators.note: over means the Scottish bank is turned back to front

parts.note: brae is Scots for a hillside or bank

explanation.surface: A Scottish bank branch in New York, far from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank of Scotland' looks like the financial institution, but it is the Scots word for a hillside, which 'over' turns round. The definition is the opposite of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonym, as the preamble requires: far off is the reverse of close at hand.
